title: Janus Infinite Faces — Network Partition and Split-Brain Authority Test

scenario.problem: A and B cannot observe each other but both retain the same pre-partition identity history.

unsafe_naive_rule: If each node continues committing because its local state was valid before the partition, the same host gains two simultaneous causal writers.

authority_rule.grant: Only a partition able to obtain a valid quorum certificate may advance to a new authority epoch/fence token for shared world effects.

bounded_local_failsafe.purpose: Prevent immediate local damage when waiting for quorum would itself be harmful.
constraints: must be pre-authorized by host constitution
must be scoped to resources physically controlled by the isolated node
must not consume or transfer an exclusive shared resource
must not create new external host obligations
must not mint a new authority epoch
must emit a pending local receipt for later reconciliation
examples: disconnect local power to prevent overheating

safety_availability_tradeoff.statement: Janus sacrifices the ability to keep writing everywhere rather than permit two partitions to become two simultaneous authors of one host's shared causal history.

ru: Два честных Януса могут стать split-brain без единой лжи.
Валидность до разрыва связи не даёт автоматического права писать общий мир после разрыва.
Для общих необратимых действий Янус предпочитает единственного писателя доступности двух писателей.
Локальный fail-safe спасает локальное состояние, но не превращается в глобальную власть.
en: Two honest Janus nodes can become split-brain without either one lying.
Pre-partition validity does not automatically grant post-partition shared commit authority.
For shared irreversible effects, Janus prefers one writer over two available writers.
Local fail-safe capability is not global authority.
